concept: Federal district court CM/ECF civil docket number

row.concept: Federal district court CM/ECF civil docket number
row.description: A federal civil-case identifier in the common division:year-cv-sequence presentation used by district-court docket systems.
row.wrong_generalization: Treating every federal docket number as a fixed-width national identifier would wrongly reject courts that omit leading zeroes or use different division and case-type conventions.

concept: Federal Rules of Civil Procedure rule number

row.concept: Federal Rules of Civil Procedure rule number
row.description: The numbered-rule component of a citation to the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure.

neighbors.concept: Federal Rules of Criminal Procedure rule number

row.wrong_generalization: Using the smallest and largest rule numbers merely observed in a sample would be wrong; the 1–86 window comes from the numbered federal civil-rule set, not sample statistics.

row.description: An abbreviated-month date token used in a Bluebook-style judicial-decision parenthetical.
row.wrong_generalization: Generalizing this as an arbitrary three-letter word plus a period would admit non-month tokens; the month component belongs to the closed legal-citation month vocabulary.

row.description: The concise pleading-title designation used to identify an original complaint or an amended complaint.
row.wrong_generalization: Treating the optional amendment mark as a general revision field would incorrectly accept ordinal amendments such as 'Second Am. Compl.', which require a different caption convention.

concept: United States Reports citation with pinpoint pages

row.concept: United States Reports citation with pinpoint pages
row.description: A Bluebook-style United States Reports citation containing an initial page followed by one or more pinpoint-page references.

neighbors.concept: United States Reports citation without pinpoint

row.wrong_generalization: Collapsing the comma-separated pages into one fixed list length would lose the fact that pinpoint references are repeatable and may contain several nonconsecutive pages.

row.description: A year-and-database identifier citation for an unpublished or database-reported judicial decision.
row.wrong_generalization: Assuming that Westlaw identifiers are always seven digits because examples often look fixed-width would wrongly reject shorter and longer valid identifier values.
